en: Saṃyutta Nikāya 32.1 (SN 32.1, PTS SN iii 254) 1. Valāhakavagga Suddhikasutta (The Simple Discourse) At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of clouds. What four? The cloud that rains down upon one place; the cloud that rains down upon two places; the cloud that rains down upon three places; the cloud that rains down everywhere. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of clouds. So too, bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons similar to clouds. What four? The person similar to a cloud that rains down upon one place; the person similar to a cloud that rains down upon two places; the person similar to a cloud that rains down upon three places; the person similar to a cloud that rains down everywhere. And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that rains down upon one place? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu develops the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving, but he does not develop the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to energy… concentration due to mind… concentration due to investigation and volitional formations of striving. He attains the destruction of the taints with the destruction of the five lower fetters. This is called a person similar to a cloud that rains down upon one place. And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that rains down upon two places? Here, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu develops the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving, but he does not develop the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to energy… concentration due to mind… concentration due to investigation and volitional formations of striving. He attains the destruction of the taints with the destruction of the five lower fetters. This is called a person similar to a cloud that rains down upon two places. And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that rains down upon three places? Here, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu develops the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving, but he does not develop the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to energy… concentration due to mind… concentration due to investigation and volitional formations of striving. He attains the destruction of the taints with the destruction of the five lower fetters. This is called a person similar to a cloud that rains down upon three places. And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that rains down everywhere? Here, bhikkhu, a bhikkhu develops the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to desire and volitional formations of striving, and he develops the basis for psychic power that possesses concentration due to energy… concentration due to mind… concentration due to investigation and volitional formations of striving. With the destruction of the taints, he realizes for himself with direct knowledge, in this very life, the taintless liberation of mind, liberation by wisdom, and having entered upon it, dwells in it. This is called a person similar to a cloud that rains down everywhere.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
"Bhikkhus, I will teach you about the deities belonging to the cloud-host.
Listen to that."
And who, monks, are the Cloud-Bodied deities?
There are, monks, the Cool-Cloud deities;
there are the Warm-Cloud deities.
There are gods who cause lightning;
there are gods who cause wind;
there are gods who cause rain.
“Monks, these are called the ‘Cloud-Bodied Devas.
The first.
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 32.2 (SN 32.2, PTS SN iii 254)
1. The Chapter on Clouds (Valāhakavagga).
Discourse on Good Conduct (Sucaritasutta).
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the Valāhakakāyika devas?
“Here, bhikkhu, someone practices good conduct by body, practices good conduct by speech, and practices good conduct by mind.”
He has heard:
"The Cloud-Bodied deities are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, following death, I might be reborn in the company of the Valāhaka-body gods!
He, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the Valāhaka-body gods.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the Valāhaka-body gods.”
The Second [Chapter].
Saṁyutta Nikāya 32.3–12 (SN 32.3, PTS SN iii 254) 1.
The Chapter on Clouds (Valāhakavagga)
The Tenfold Discourse on the Assistance of the Gift of Sītavalāhaka.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the Sītavalāhaka devas?
“Bhikkhu, here someone practices good conduct by body, good conduct by speech, and good conduct by mind.
He has heard:”
‘The Sītavalāhaka devas are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn into the company of the Sītavalāhaka devas!’
Thus he gives food...
[and so on] ...he gives lighting.
With the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn in the company of the Sītavalāhaka devas.
“Monk, this is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn in the company of the Sītavalāhaka devas.
The twelfth [sutta].
*Saṃyutta Nikāya* 32.13–52 (SN 32.13, PTS SN iii 255)
1. The Chapter on Clouds (Valāhakavagga).
The Discourse on the Benefit of the Gift of the Hot-Cloud (Uṇhavalāhakadānūpakārasutta).
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why here someone, with the breakup of the body, after death,
[is reborn] among the Uṇhavalāhaka devas … among the Abbhavalāhaka devas …?”
“...is he reborn in the company of the Vātavalāhaka gods... or the Vassavalāhaka gods?
“Here, bhikkhu, a certain person practices good conduct by body, practices good conduct by speech, and practices good conduct by mind.”
He has heard:
"The rain-cloud deities are long-lived, beautiful, and abound in happiness.
It occurs to him:
‘Oh, that after the breakup of the body, after death, I might be reborn in the company of the Vassavalāhaka rain-cloud deities!
He gives food... [and so on] ...he gives lighting.
Thus, with the breakup of the body, after death, he is reborn into the company of the Vassavalāhaka rain-cloud deities.
This, monk, is the cause, this is the condition, by which someone here, with the breakup of the body, after death, is reborn into the company of the Vassavalāhaka rain-cloud deities.
(Fifty-second)

Saṁyutta Nikāya 32.53 The Cold Cloud Discourse At Sāvatthī. “Bhikkhus, suppose there were a cold cloud, and from that cold cloud a cold rain fell. That cold rain would fall on a cold mountain. There, a cold mist would arise, and it would be cold, harsh, and painful to the touch. So too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is cold, harsh, and painful to associate with, he arouses a cold mist within himself, and it is cold, harsh, and painful to the touch. “And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu cold, harsh, and painful to associate with, arousing a cold mist within himself that is cold, harsh, and painful to the touch? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is angry and bears ill will; he is corrupt in his resolves and has evil wishes; he is envious and miserly; he is crafty and deceitful; he is obstinate and proud; he has evil friends, evil companions, and evil comrades; he is lazy and muddle-minded; he is unconcentrated and has a wandering mind; he is ignorant and lacks wisdom. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is cold, harsh, and painful to associate with, arousing a cold mist within himself that is cold, harsh, and painful to the touch. “Suppose, bhikkhus, there were a hot cloud, and from that hot cloud a hot rain fell. That hot rain would fall on a hot mountain. There, a hot mist would arise, and it would be hot, harsh, and painful to the touch. So too, bhikkhus, when a bhikkhu is hot, harsh, and painful to associate with, he arouses a hot mist within himself, and it is hot, harsh, and painful to the touch. “And how, bhikkhus, is a bhikkhu hot, harsh, and painful to associate with, arousing a hot mist within himself that is hot, harsh, and painful to the touch? Here, bhikkhus, a bhikkhu is not angry and does not bear ill will; he is pure in his resolves and has wholesome wishes; he is not envious and not miserly; he is not crafty and not deceitful; he is not obstinate and not proud; he has good friends, good companions, and good comrades; he is energetic and possesses mindfulness; he is concentrated and possesses a unified mind; he is wise and possesses wisdom. It is in this way, bhikkhus, that a bhikkhu is hot, harsh, and painful to associate with, arousing a hot mist within himself that is hot, harsh, and painful to the touch.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why it sometimes becomes cold?”
“Bhikkhu, there are gods called the Cool Clouds.
When it occurs to them, ‘What if we were to dwell in our own delight? then, in accordance with that mental aspiration of theirs, it becomes cool.”
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, why at times it becomes cold.
(The Fifty-Third Discourse) Saṁyutta Nikāya 32.54 (SN 32.54, PTS SN iii 256)
1. The Chapter on Clouds (Valāhakavagga).
The Discourse on the Hot Cloud (Uṇhavalāhakasutta).
Setting at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the condition, why it sometimes becomes hot?
“There are, bhikkhu, certain deities called the ‘hot-cloud’ deities.”
When it occurs to them,
‘What if we were to dwell according to our own pleasure?’, then, following that mental aspiration of theirs,
it becomes hot. This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, why at times it becomes hot.”
Fifty-fourth.
Saṁyutta Nikāya 32.55 (SN 32.55, PTS SN iii 256) 1.
The Chapter on Clouds (Valāhakavagga)
The Discourse on the Clouds that Bring Rain. At Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
“Venerable sir, what is the cause, what is the reason, why at times there is cloud?
“Bhikkhu, there are gods called ‘cloud-producers.
When it occurs to them thus:”
‘What if we were to dwell according to our own pleasure? Following that mental aspiration of theirs, a cloud appears.
This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, why at times a cloud appears.
(Fifty-fifth)

Saṃyutta Nikāya 32.56 (SN 32.56, PTS SN iii 256) 1. Valāhakavagga Vātavalāhakasutta (The Wind-Cloud Discourse) “Bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of clouds. What four? The cloud that rains down wind, the cloud that rains down rain, the cloud that thunders, and the cloud that flashes. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of clouds. So too, bhikkhus, there are these four kinds of persons similar to clouds. What four? The person similar to a cloud that rains down wind, the person similar to a cloud that rains down rain, the person similar to a cloud that thunders, and the person similar to a cloud that flashes. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of persons similar to clouds. (1) “And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that rains down wind? Here, bhikkhus, one person has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, but he dwells pursuing what is connected with the household life; he dwells pursuing the acquisition of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. He is one who speaks in praise of such pursuits and encourages others in them. Just as the cloud that rains down wind does not bring much benefit to many people, so too this person is similar to a cloud that rains down wind. This is called a person similar to a cloud that rains down wind. (2) “And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that rains down rain? Here, bhikkhus, one person has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and he dwells pursuing what is connected with the household life; he dwells pursuing the acquisition of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. But he is one who does not speak in praise of such pursuits nor encourage others in them. Just as the cloud that rains down rain brings much benefit to many people, so too this person is similar to a cloud that rains down rain. This is called a person similar to a cloud that rains down rain. (3) “And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that thunders? Here, bhikkhus, one person has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and he dwells pursuing what is connected with the household life; he dwells pursuing the acquisition of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. He does not speak in praise of such pursuits nor encourage others in them, yet he does not abandon those very things by which one would be called a lay follower. Just as the cloud that thunders does not bring much benefit to many people, so too this person is similar to a cloud that thunders. This is called a person similar to a cloud that thunders. (4) “And how, bhikkhus, is a person similar to a cloud that flashes? Here, bhikkhus, one person has gone forth from the household life into homelessness, and he dwells pursuing what is connected with the household life; he dwells pursuing the acquisition of robes, almsfood, lodgings, and medicinal requisites for the sick. He does not speak in praise of such pursuits nor encourage others in them, and he abandons those very things by which one would be called a lay follower. Just as the cloud that flashes brings much benefit to many people, so too this person is similar to a cloud that flashes. This is called a person similar to a cloud that flashes. These, bhikkhus, are the four kinds of persons similar to clouds.”
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Sitting to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
"What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why at times there is wind?"
“Bhikkhu, there are gods called the Wind-Clouds.
When it occurs to them, ‘What if we were to dwell in our own delight? then, in accordance with that mental aspiration of theirs, wind arises.”
“This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, by which at times there is wind.
(The Fifty-sixth Discourse). *Saṃyutta Nikāya* 32.57.
1. The Chapter on Clouds:
The Discourse on Rain-Clouds.
The setting was at Sāvatthī.
Seated to one side, that bhikkhu said this to the Blessed One:
"What, venerable sir, is the cause, what is the reason, why at times the rain falls?
"There are, bhikkhu, certain deities known as the rain-cloud deities."
When it occurs to them, “What if we were to dwell according to our own pleasure? then, in accordance with that mental aspiration of theirs, the rain falls.
This, bhikkhu, is the cause, this is the condition, why at times the rain falls.”
The fifty-seventh [discourse].
The Sattapaññāsa Sutta is finished.
The first chapter, the Valāhaka Vagga.
Its summary verse:
The pure [precepts], good conduct,
giving, assistance, and wisdom.
Cold, heat, and cloud,
wind, rain, and clouds.
The Connected Discourses on Clouds are complete.
